result.title: Accounting Policy Manual - posting authority, support, approvals
result.text:
HALVARD SYSTEMS - ACCOUNTING POLICY MANUAL (excerpt), effective 2026-01-01
Applies to Halvard Systems Inc. (US), Halvard Systems Ltd (UK), Halvard Systems GmbH (DE).

1. Posting authority. Senior accountants may post manual journal entries up to USD 10,000
   per entry (local-currency entries are measured at the month-end rate of the entry month).
   Any entry above USD 10,000 must be routed to the Controller with an approval request
   (request_approval) immediately after posting; it remains pending until approved.
   Splitting one transaction into several entries to stay under the threshold is prohibited.
2. Support. Every journal entry must have its supporting document(s) attached. An entry
   without support is not a valid entry.
3. Capitalization. Individual equipment purchases of USD 2,500 or more (local-currency
   equivalent at the month-end rate) are capitalized to 1500 Computer Equipment and
   depreciated over 36 months beginning the month after acquisition.
4. Prepaids. Payments covering services or events in future periods (more than one month
   out, or spanning more than one month) above USD 1,000 are recorded as prepaid (1210
   Prepaid Software for software, 1220 Prepaid Insurance for insurance, 1200 Prepaid Expenses
   for everything else, including deposits for future events) and expensed straight-line over
   the coverage period starting the month coverage begins, or when the event occurs.
5. Accruals. Expenses are recorded in the period the goods or services are received. Services
   received but not yet invoiced at month-end are accrued to 2100 Accrued Expenses using the
   best available evidence (vendor statements, approved timesheets, engagement terms).
   Quotes or proposals for future work are not liabilities.
6. Revenue. Revenue is recognized under ASC 606 per the contract terms. Deferred revenue
   (2200) is released as performance obligations are satisfied. Usage earned but not yet
   invoiced is recorded to 1300 Unbilled Receivables.
7. Customer credits. SLA credits are issued only per contract terms and verified uptime data
   (see the monthly uptime report). Credits are recorded as a reduction of the related revenue.
8. Cash application. Customer receipts are applied to invoices per remittance advice. Receipts
   that cannot be matched to an open invoice remain in 2950 Unapplied Cash.
9. FX. Monetary balances denominated in a currency other than the entity's functional
   currency are remeasured at the month-end rate; gains/losses go to 6950 FX Gain/Loss.
   Intercompany charges are recorded by the receiving entity at the month-end rate of the
   month charged.
10. Payroll. Returned payroll deposits are recorded to 2150 Accrued Payroll & Unclaimed
   Wages until reissued. Unpaid wages at month-end are accrued to 2150.
11. Exceptions. Items that cannot be supported must be reported via flag_exception. Never
   post an entry to force a reconciliation or to make balances agree.
12. Periods. January and February 2026 are closed. March 2026 is open.

args.text:
MEMO – March 2026 Revenue Recognition: Dunmore Foods and Harlow Freight (US entity)
Prepared by: Senior Accountant, 2026-04-03

SUMMARY OF ENTRIES POSTED
1. JE-00311 (2026-03-31, US): Dr 2200 Deferred Revenue 5,000.00 / Cr 4000 Subscription Revenue 5,000.00 – Dunmore Foods March rev rec. Support: DOC-0002, DOC-0155, DOC-0156.
2. JE-00312 (2026-03-31, US): Dr 1300 Unbilled Receivables 5,000.00 / Cr 4100 Usage Revenue 5,000.00 – Harlow Freight March usage. Support: DOC-0001, DOC-0206.
Both entries are USD 5,000 (below the USD 10,000 posting-authority threshold in Policy §1), so no controller approval request is required. Entries were NOT split; each customer is a single, separately supported transaction.

DUNMORE FOODS – ASC 606 ANALYSIS
Original contract (DOC-0002): Core platform subscription, USD 48,000 for 2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31, invoiced annually in advance (INV-1001, DOC-0005; recorded to deferred revenue in JE-00012, cash received JE-00079). Service is provided evenly over the term – a stand-ready obligation satisfied over time, recognized straight-line at 48,000/12 = USD 4,000 per month. January and February were recognized in JE-00111 and JE-00215 (4,000 each).

Amendment No. 1 (DOC-0155), effective 2026-03-01: adds the Analytics module for 2026-03-01 to 2026-12-31 at USD 1,000/month (USD 10,000 total), invoiced in advance on 2026-03-01 (INV-1052, DOC-0156; deferred in JE-00229). The amendment states the Analytics module is a distinct service priced at its standalone selling price, and that core subscription terms are unchanged.

Conclusion: Under ASC 606-10-25-12, a contract modification is accounted for as a SEPARATE CONTRACT when (a) the scope increases because of the addition of promised services that are distinct, and (b) the price increases by an amount reflecting the standalone selling price of the added services. Both criteria are met per the contract language. Therefore the original core subscription is neither reallocated nor re-measured (no cumulative catch-up and no prospective blending of the remaining core deferred balance with the new module). The Analytics module is recognized on its own straight-line over its 10-month term (Mar–Dec 2026) at 10,000/10 = USD 1,000 per month.

March 2026 Dunmore revenue = 4,000 (core) + 1,000 (Analytics) = USD 5,000.

Deferred revenue roll-forward check (2200, US): opening Mar balance 40,000 (48,000 – 8,000) + 10,000 INV-1052 = 50,000 before rev rec; after JE-00311 = USD 45,000, of which 36,000 is core (9 months remaining) and 9,000 is Analytics (9 months remaining). Ties.

HARLOW FREIGHT – ASC 606 ANALYSIS
Contract (DOC-0001): USD 0.10 per shipment processed, no minimum, invoiced quarterly in arrears (Q1 invoice issued in early April). The performance obligation is satisfied as each shipment is processed. This is usage-based variable consideration allocated entirely to the period of usage (ASC 606-10-55-65 / 606-10-32-40 variable consideration allocated to the distinct service period), so revenue is recognized in the month the shipments occur regardless of billing timing.

March usage report (DOC-0206): 50,000 shipments x USD 0.10 = USD 5,000.00. Because the Q1 invoice is not issued until April, the amount is recorded to 1300 Unbilled Receivables (contract asset) per Policy §6, consistent with the January (JE-00112, 4,120) and February (JE-00210, 4,480) treatment.

Unbilled roll-forward (1300, US): 4,120 + 4,480 + 5,000 = USD 13,600 at 2026-03-31 for Harlow (41,200 + 44,800 + 50,000 = 136,000 Q1 shipments x 0.10). When the Q1 invoice is issued in April, AR should be debited and 1300 credited for 13,600 – recommend AR confirm the April invoice agrees to this amount.

CHECKLIST
US "Revenue recognition" item set to in_progress – Dunmore Foods and Harlow Freight are complete; other US customers (if any) remain to be reviewed by the revenue accountant.

EXCEPTIONS
None. All amounts fully supported by contracts, invoices and usage reports; no exceptions flagged.
